newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bunds end rock steady, focus on Ifo report.
newsitem.headline: Bunds end rock steady, focus on Ifo report.

text.p: Bunds stagnated around opening levels almost all day on Wednesday, taking a breather from a steep decline on Tuesday and unmoved by Bundesbank comments about the economy.
The DTB September Bund future was up a single basis point at 101.34 in late afternoon trade after having traded in a range 101.09 and 101.44.

Traders shrugged off the Bundesbank's monthly report for June which saw no inflationary pressures and comments from central bank President Hans Tietmeyer who expressed satisfaction with the Amsterdam EU summit.
Traders said the main focus will be on the Ifo research institute's business sentiment survey due on Thursday.
German M3 money supply, which is also due sometime this week, has lost some of its importance in the market, which has placed additional weight on the Ifo report, they said.
The benchmark 10-year Bund was slightly higher in late trade at 102.04 compared with 101.97. The yield on the cash Bund stood at 5.72 percent.
Analysts said they expected the long-end of the German yield curve to continue to perform well, helping to further flatten the spread between two- and 10-year maturities.
By late in the afternoon, the spread stood at 225 basis points, down from a gap of over 300 basis points last week.
The spread between Bunds and Treasuries narrowed three basis points on the day to 80 after U.S. productivity data were released in the afternoon.
